content: {"id": "c5b83cb3-a5fb-45c5-b407-e401de94e595", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Our application gets AccessDeniedException when it calls InvokeModel on Bedrock. Is this something we can fix in our IAM policy, or is it coming from somewhere else?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "152ed1c8-cfd6-482a-90ae-e3fc10ff678f", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "It could be either. The exact error message usually shows which one it is.

**Fixable in your IAM policy**
- The message says "...is not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel on resource: ... because no identity-based policy allows the bedrock:InvokeModel action". Add `bedrock:InvokeModel` (and `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` if you stream) on the model ARN to the calling role.
- You call the model through a **cross-region inference profile** (model IDs like `us.anthropic...`). The role needs permission on the inference profile ARN and on the underlying foundation-model ARN in every region the profile can route to. Missing the foundation-model ARNs is a common cause.

**Coming from somewhere else**
- The message says "explicit deny in a service control policy" (or a resource control policy). An org admin has to change this, and your IAM policy can't override it.
- The message says "explicit deny in a permissions boundary" or "session policy". The boundary or session policy has to allow the action.
- The message says "You don't have access to the model with the specified model ID". This is model access, not IAM. The model may not be enabled in that account or region, or a first-time use-case form or Marketplace subscription may be pending. Subscribing also needs `aws-marketplace:Subscribe`-type permissions for whoever enables it.
- A VPC endpoint policy for Bedrock runtime may be blocking the call.
- The call may be going to the wrong region, or the app may be using different credentials than you expect, such as a different assumed role or account.

**Quickest way to tell**
1. Read the full error text. The clause after "because..." names the source.
2. Check the role ARN in the message. It should be the one you expect.
3. Look up the failed `InvokeModel` event in CloudTrail. It shows the principal, region, and model.

If you paste the full error message, I can tell you which case it is. I can also search CloudTrail in your account for the denied calls if you give me the approximate time and the role or app name.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
